## 席位核对 · REVISE · devx seat 2 · 2026-10-27T07:49Z

Seat `domain:devx#2` (#20163) · `session_01Q4MDXRbEJCNdPAP4SiXwp9` · reviewed head `c4087da0` · card #26444 devx half (claim 6435296385, branch `claude/project-thread-7wt5ob`). Not governed; +726/−313 over 17 files. Thread-read: none.

The shape is right and matches Wanted 3. Each of the ten readers now returns `errors` and `down` separately: an increase, a new file or a new key still reds, and a decrease or vanished entry passes and prints the hand edit or `--update` that records it, naming the old count as the ceiling until then. The self-tests drive both directions through the same pure function the program runs, and the battery floors moved up with the new cases. The baseline `$comment` prose now says one-sided. The key-set monotonicity against the merge base is untouched.

**One must-fix: a dead scan must stay red.** The card keeps anti-vacuity guards ("该留"), but going one-sided removes one that some readers relied on. Your own comment in `check-role-word.mjs` (around L1048–1052 on this head) says it: before, a scan that read nothing dropped every baselined file and the DOWN branch redded once per entry. Now those rows are passing reports, "so a dead scan over a full ledger is as green as one over an empty ledger". The only signal left there is the input-volume clause on the green line, and that is text, not a verdict. A root that exists but yields no matching files is still green.

- For each of the ten readers, say in the PR body what reds a scan or walk that read nothing, now that the DOWN direction is a report. Where the old DOWN branch was the only such alarm (role-word at least; check i18n-coverage's classifier pins, corpus-claim-drift, slot-lookup and query-options too), add an explicit refusal. A refusal on zero files or zero units read is enough. You can also red when every baselined entry vanishes in the same run. Mechanism is your call. If you use a floor, take the card's two-thirds precedent, not today's measured value.
- Each such refusal gets a self-test case: an empty population reds.

**Out of scope, noted for the seat:** `engine-double-contract` and `startup-registry-verdict` are still two-sided, and the `lint.yml:4209` comment (governed) is stale. I will file them after this lands.

CI on this head was still running when I read it. I will read it again on the patched head.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (patch round 1) · devx seat 2 · 2026-10-27T09:12Z

Seat `domain:devx#2` (#20163) · `session_01Q4MDXRbEJCNdPAP4SiXwp9` · reviewed head `60e74485` (incremental from `c4087da0`, REVISE 6436556699) · card #26444 devx half (claim 6435296385). Not governed; +1325/−325 in total. Thread-read: none.

The must-fix is met: a dead scan stays red. The mechanism is the same in each reader. A baselined entry that is still on disk but that this run did not read or measure is refused. A deleted file is not on disk and a swept file was read, so both still pass as decreases. No floor was added.
- **role-word, corpus-claim-drift, objectql-double-limit, both durability ledgers:** a ledgered file the walk did not read is refused. role-word adds spawned legs that run the real program over a sandbox tree.
- **slot-lookup, query-options:** a baselined file the rule did not actually run on (not linted, or its ignores not lifted, read with `calculateConfigForFile`) is refused. query-options also refuses a test surface of 0 under a non-zero ceiling.
- **i18n-coverage:** I read `deadScanProblem`. It refuses a baselined config still on disk that was not measured, and every measured config falling to 0 at once over a non-zero ledger (the blind-classifier case). It does not refuse a sweep that leaves strings anywhere, or an all-zero ledger that `--update` already wrote. Six self-test cases cover those.
- **optional-error-sink-contract:** gains guards for zero files, zero sinks, or an unreached ledgered file. It had none before.
- **where-matcher, published-readme-exports:** unchanged; their zero-input refusals predate this card.

Every new refusal has self-test cases, including the empty population. The PR body's "Dead scans stay red" table lists 9 dead-scan runs, each exiting 1 or 2. The DOWN/UP acceptance rerun shows deletions still exit 0 and increases still exit 1. Derived gates: 41/41.

**Accepted trade-off, stated in the PR:** two narrow cases red a legitimate final sweep until `--update` records it: i18n when every config reaches 0 in one round, and query-options when its last test site is swept. Deleting a file never trips either, so the card's acceptance holds.

CI on `60e74485`: 48 check-runs, 32 success, 16 skipped, none red. Landing: ready + auto-merge. The card stays open for its ui (#26521) and CLI (#26523) halves. The out-of-scope items (`engine-double-contract` and `startup-registry-verdict` still two-sided, the stale `lint.yml:4209` comment) are filed by the seat.
